title: Britain gets experimental drug from Japan to bolster hantavirus response - DD News

analysis.time: The UK Health Security Agency reported the hantavirus outbreak on Monday, October 3, 2026. The drug favipiravir was delivered over the weekend, and the outbreak is linked to the Hondius cruise liner which docked in Rotterdam on Monday, October 3, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak is linked to the Hondius cruise liner, which docked at the Dutch port of Rotterdam. The affected population includes eight confirmed cases and two probable cases, with three deaths reported in the UK.
analysis.event: Britain received experimental favipiravir supplies from Japan to support its hantavirus response, as confirmed by the UK Health Security Agency. The drug is not licensed in the UK but is being considered for experimental use in treating severe hantavirus infections.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: There are eight confirmed cases and two probable cases of hantavirus, with three deaths. The outbreak involves the Andes virus, which is the only strain known to spread between people, though typically only after close and prolonged contact. The risk of wider transmission in the UK is described as very low.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The UK Health Security Agency accepted the drug delivery, but no details about the number of doses were disclosed. The drug is considered experimental for hantavirus treatment, and there is no internationally established clinical protocol for its routine use. The World Health Organization has not identified changes that would make the virus more transmissible or severe.

analysis.brief_en: Britain has received experimental favipiravir supplies from Japan to support its response to a hantavirus outbreak linked to the Hondius cruise liner. The UK Health Security Agency confirmed the drug's delivery over the weekend, though it remains unlicensed in the UK and is considered experimental for hantavirus treatment. The outbreak involves the Andes virus, which is the only strain known to spread between people, typically after close and prolonged contact. There are eight confirmed cases and two probable cases, with three deaths reported. The risk of wider transmission in the UK is described as very low. The drug works by blocking a key enzyme that many viruses need to multiply, and its use for hantavirus is not standard care. While the World Health Organization has not identified changes that would make the virus more transmissible or severe, there is no internationally established clinical protocol for favipiravir's routine use against hantavirus. The UKHSA emphasized that the drug is likely to be used for severe infections early on, based on limited lab and animal study evidence.

analysis.location_and_population: The event occurred on the cruise ship MV Hondius, which was docked off the coast of Tenerife in the Canary Islands, Spain. The affected population includes over 140 people on the ship, with fourteen Spanish nationals being the first group evacuated.

analysis.time: The suspected hantavirus outbreak was reported on May 6, 2026, with the confirmed cases linked to the cluster rising to five. The event date is May 6, 2026, and the two new confirmed cases were among people medically evacuated from the ship on that day. The ship departed Cape Verde on May 6, 2026, heading to Spain's Canary Islands.
analysis.location_and_population: The suspected outbreak occurred aboard the cruise ship MV Hondius, which departed Cape Verde on May 6, 2026, heading to Spain's Canary Islands. The affected population includes passengers and crew, with a focus on older individuals due to their higher risk of severe illness.
analysis.event: Confirmed hantavirus cases linked to a suspected cluster on the cruise ship MV Hondius have risen to five, as reported by the World Health Organization (WHO). The WHO confirmed the cases and stated that there may be some person-to-person spread in the outbreak. The type of virus was identified as Andes hantavirus.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: There are five confirmed hantavirus cases, with three deaths recorded. Two of the evacuated patients are in serious condition, and one is asymptomatic but a close contact of a deceased individual. The WHO stated that the overall public health risk remains low. The ship had nearly 150 people on board, and Spanish health authorities will take over further investigations.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: WHO officials are working with the ship's operators and national health authorities to monitor the health of passengers and crew. Two infectious disease physicians from the Netherlands have been sent to the ship to provide medical care. The ship's evacuation plan was updated to send all evacuated individuals to the Netherlands. The Canary Islands regional government opposes docking the ship due to insufficient information and public safety concerns.

WHO officials are collaborating with the ship's operators and national health authorities to monitor the situation and provide medical follow-up. Two infectious disease physicians from the Netherlands have been sent to the ship to assist with care. The Canary Islands regional government has expressed opposition to docking the ship due to insufficient information and public safety concerns. The overall public health risk is deemed low by the WHO, and further investigations will be conducted by Spanish health authorities upon the ship's arrival.
